math_checks.outcome: I checked the proposed obstruction for the ordinary category of small groupoids with strict functors. Let G=S_3 and H={e,(12)}. The subgroup inclusion BH -> BG is a monomorphism: on the unique object it is injective, and on arrows it is an injective group homomorphism, so equal composites force equal functors. If t:1 -> Omega were a subobject classifier and chi:BG -> Omega classified this inclusion, the nonempty pullback would force chi(*)=t(*). Its automorphism group would then be the kernel of G -> Aut_Omega(t(*)), hence a normal subgroup of G. But H is not normal: conjugating (12) by (123) gives (23), outside H. This contradicts the classifier property, confirming the suggested absence of a subobject classifier and thus an obstruction to being a topos in this ordinary categorical interpretation. I did not investigate alternative 2-categorical meanings or prove the separate proposed homotopy-group computation.
